name: Renaissance

global_influences.evidence: Renaissance's core genre profile combines reggae, jazz and soft rock, with jazz manifesting in improvisational guitar/keyboard solos and harmonic extensions beyond standard rock progressions, and blues influences contributing gritty, emotive lead guitar phrasing — an unusually eclectic combination relative to the harder-rock-dominant mainstream of the era.

local_adaptation_notes: Formed in 1985 by Naquib Khan and Pilu Khan after departing Souls, Renaissance directly continued the founding-generation rock lineage while distinguishing itself through reggae and jazz textures rather than straight hard rock; the 1998 album Ekattorer Renaissance is a dedicated tribute to Liberation War-era songs from Swadhin Bangla Betar Kendra (the wartime clandestine radio station), directly linking the band's musicianship to national historical memory in a manner paralleling Ark's and Cryptic Fate's later work.
sound_evolution_summary: Founding period (1985): formed by Souls alumni Naquib Khan and Pilu Khan with Rumi, Moto, Bogi and Reza. Breakthrough period (1988): self-titled debut album, featuring 'Bhalo Lage Jochna Rate,' shifted Bangladeshi band music toward more melody-driven, jazz/pop/rock-blended composition. Consolidation period (1993–2004): Tritiyo Bishwo (1993), the Liberation War tribute album Ekattorer Renaissance (1998), and Ekush Shotoke Renaissance (2004) demonstrated stylistic versatility spanning 1960s rock, heavy metal, rock and roll, and regional dialects.
concert_culture_notes: Performed at the BAMBA multi-band Eid celebration concert at Jamuna Future Park alongside Warfaze, Maqsood O Dhaka, Nemesis and Mechanix (see data/concerts/bamba-eid-concert-jamuna-future-park.json), indicating continued active participation in the mainstream festival circuit decades after formation.
listener_community_notes: As a direct offshoot of Souls, Renaissance is part of the same founding-generation genealogical cluster as Souls, LRB (via Ayub Bachchu) and other 1970s-80s-rooted acts, appealing to listeners who value melodic, genre-blending musicianship over straightforward hard rock.
